title: Export job performance benchmarks (Usage Insights) — CSV/JSON limits + recommended guardrails
content:
Redwood Inference — Engineering / Observability

Document type: PDF-style note (export-job benchmarking results)
Project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
Focus area: Export job generation (CSV + JSON)

Author: Allison Grant (SRE/Observability)
Contributors: Mei Lin, Nadia Rahman, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams
Last updated: 2026-02-21

---

1) Summary (what we learned)

We benchmarked the new Usage Insights export job pipeline (Create Export → async job → download CSV/JSON) under realistic customer queries and under adversarial “wide” queries that produce high row counts.

Key findings:
- Export generation time grows roughly linearly with (a) row count and (b) number of columns enabled, but has sharp nonlinearities when we exceed memory thresholds and fall back to multiple buffered chunks.
- JSON exports are 2–4x slower than CSV for equivalent data and typically 1.7–3.2x larger on disk.
- The dominant failure mode is worker timeout / job lease expiration when queries span long time ranges and include high-cardinality routes (or route normalization collapses into “other” but still produces many per-model breakdown rows).
- With conservative limits and “sane defaults” (7d range, filters required, bounded rows/bytes), we can meet a practical SLO: 95% of exports ready in < 90s, and 99% in < 180s, even with moderate concurrency.

Recommended guardrails (proposed GA defaults):
- Default export range: 7 days
- Max export range: 31 days (hard cap)
- Max rows returned (post-aggregation): 250,000 rows (hard cap)
- Max file size (uncompressed):
  - CSV: 50 MB
  - JSON: 100 MB
- Max job runtime: 180 seconds (worker hard timeout), with early “fail fast” if predicted size exceeds caps
- Concurrency: 10 running export jobs per region per cluster (configurable), with per-org throttling
- Require at least one scoping filter beyond time range (e.g., environment OR region OR deployment_mode) for ranges > 7d

Status: These guardrails are sufficient to prevent the timeouts observed in internal load testing (see incident-adjacent notes below) while keeping exports useful for Finance/FinOps workflows.

---

2) Test setup

2.1 Code under test
- Export job service + download endpoint implementation (ref: GitHub:redwood/pr-15485)
- Audit logging + RBAC checks (ref: GitHub:redwood/pr-15492)

2.2 Dataset
We tested against aggregated Usage Insights datasets (route/model rollups), not raw request logs.
- Primary table(s): hourly and daily aggregates used by “top routes” and “route detail → model breakdown”
- Typical row shape:
  - Dimensions: org_id, project_id, time_bucket, route, model, region, environment, deployment_mode
  - Metrics: total_cost, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cached_output_tokens, request_count, error_count, p50_ms, p95_ms

2.3 Environments
- Staging cluster (us-west) with production-like node types, but smaller cache and smaller read replica pool
- One ad-hoc run on a prod-readonly replica with synthetic org_id to validate query planner behavior (no customer data exported)

2.4 Load and concurrency
- Single-job microbenchmarks to measure baseline time/row
- Concurrency tests at 1, 5, 10, 20 concurrent export jobs
- Mixed workload tests: 70% “normal” (<= 7d, filtered), 30% “wide” (>= 30d, fewer filters)

2.5 Output formats
- CSV: UTF-8, header row, RFC4180-ish quoting
- JSON: array-of-objects (NOT NDJSON), intended for Finance scripts / import

Note: We did not test compression in this iteration. We assume uncompressed file caps for predictable customer experience and to simplify browser downloads. If we introduce gzip later, we should keep the uncompressed cap as the primary safety check.

---

3) Results

3.1 Single-job benchmarks (baseline)

All numbers below represent end-to-end “job runtime” = query + serialization + write to object storage + mark job ready.
Download time is excluded (depends on client).

A) Typical export: 7d, filtered by environment=prod, region=us-west, includes route+model breakdown
- Rows: ~18,000
- Columns: 18
- Output sizes:
  - CSV: ~6.2 MB
  - JSON: ~14.8 MB
- Runtime (seconds):
  - CSV: p50 9.4s / p95 18.7s
  - JSON: p50 22.1s / p95 41.6s

B) Medium export: 31d, filtered by environment=prod, region=us-west
- Rows: ~92,000
- Columns: 18
- Output sizes:
  - CSV: ~31 MB
  - JSON: ~71 MB
- Runtime (seconds):
  - CSV: p50 41.8s / p95 79.5s
  - JSON: p50 96.7s / p95 168.2s

C) Wide export (stress): 31d, environment=prod ONLY (no region filter), high route cardinality org
- Rows: ~210,000
- Columns: 18
- Output sizes:
  - CSV: ~68 MB
  - JSON: ~151 MB
- Runtime (seconds):
  - CSV: p50 122.4s / p95 206.9s
  - JSON: p50 248.2s / p95 > 300s (timeouts)

Interpretation:
- The stress case is representative of what triggered timeouts in internal load tests: large time window + insufficient filters + high cardinality.
- JSON format is disproportionately impacted and crosses practical limits earlier.

3.2 Concurrency impact

We ran the “Typical export” profile (A) at increasing concurrency. The query layer stayed stable up to 10 concurrent jobs; at 20, the database CPU and IO saturation increased p95 significantly.

Typical export (7d, filtered) runtime by concurrency:
- 1 concurrent: CSV p95 ~19s
- 5 concurrent: CSV p95 ~28s
- 10 concurrent: CSV p95 ~44s
- 20 concurrent: CSV p95 ~96s (unacceptable)

Observations:
- The export service can serialize quickly, but the DB becomes the bottleneck under high concurrency.
- Per-org throttling is necessary; otherwise a single org can starve others.

3.3 Failure modes observed

1) Worker timeout (hard timeout / lease expiration)
- Most common in JSON exports for medium-to-wide ranges.
- Correlated with file sizes > ~100MB and/or row counts > ~200k.

2) Object storage write stalls
- Rare; seen once during 20-concurrent run. Retried successfully.
- Suggests we should treat storage write as retryable and keep partial uploads from being downloadable.

3) “Success but unusable” (client pain)
- CSV files above ~50MB are technically downloadable but often too slow in-browser and frequently opened in Excel/Sheets with poor outcomes.
- Finance users usually prefer smaller exports per environment/region and/or per week.

---

4) Recommended guardrails (proposed for GA)

These are intentionally conservative. The goal is predictable success, not maximum possible extraction.

4.1 Limits

Hard caps (enforced at export creation time if possible; otherwise fail fast at start of job):
- Max time range: 31 days
- Max rows: 250,000 rows
- Max file size:
  - CSV: 50 MB
  - JSON: 100 MB
- Max runtime: 180 seconds

Soft caps (UI warnings + suggest narrower filters):
- If estimated rows > 150,000: show “Large export” warning and recommend adding region/environment filters
- If time range > 7 days and no additional filter selected: block and require at least one of {environment, region, deployment_mode}

4.2 Defaults
- Default time range: last 7 days
- Default granularity: daily (hourly only when range <= 72 hours)
- Default format: CSV (JSON available but not the default)

4.3 Concurrency / rate limiting
- Global per-region cap: 10 running jobs
- Per-org cap: 2 running jobs, 10 queued (beyond that: 429 / “too many export jobs”)
- API rate limit: protect export creation endpoint (to prevent spam / accidental loops)

4.4 Query cost controls
- Require org_id + project_id scope (RBAC) always
- For ranges > 7d, require at least one extra scoping filter (environment OR region OR deployment_mode)
- Enforce stable sort + keyset pagination internally (even if file is single deliverable) to avoid massive in-memory buffers

4.5 File format recommendations
- Keep JSON as array-of-objects for now (most script-friendly), but consider NDJSON later to enable streaming and partial consumption.
- Reserve any schema additions for a versioned schema header in CSV (see schema versioning thread). Until then: keep fields stable.

---

5) Proposed user-facing messaging (Console + docs)

Console UI copy suggestions:
- “Exports are intended for operational and finance reporting. For large orgs, we recommend filtering by environment and region.”
- “Large exports may take several minutes. Maximum range is 31 days.”

Failure error messages:
- If over size limit: “Export too large. Reduce time range or add filters (environment/region).”
- If predicted over row limit: “Export would exceed 250k rows. Narrow the request or export a smaller subset.”

Docs troubleshooting bullets:
- “If your export fails, try: (1) last 7 days, (2) filter to a region, (3) export CSV instead of JSON.”
- “Invoice reconciliation: exports reflect telemetry attribution and may differ from invoice timing; see known issues.”

---

6) Incident-adjacent notes (internal load test)

During an internal 20-concurrent run (mix of normal + wide exports), we saw:
- Elevated export job failures due to timeout
- Increased API p95 for insights endpoints (shared database resources)

Mitigations validated by this benchmark:
- Concurrency caps + per-org throttles materially reduce p95 and failures.
- Hard size and row caps prevent pathological jobs.

Reference: Slack:eng-sre/thread-1739288444

---

7) Implementation notes / follow-ups

Already in progress / proposed tasks:
- Add “estimated size/rows” preflight using EXPLAIN row estimates + historical density heuristics (owner: Mei Lin)
- Add metrics:
  - export_job_runtime_seconds (p50/p95)
  - export_job_rows
  - export_job_bytes
  - export_job_failures_by_reason (timeout, too_large, rbac, unknown)
- Ensure audit log includes:
  - who, org/project scope, filters, format, time range, result (success/failure), file size

Open questions:
- Should we allow >31 days only for Dedicated/Private customers via support enablement?
  - Recommendation: not for GA; keep a backdoor flag for SE/support with explicit approval.
- Do we need compression?
  - Recommendation: not required for GA; revisit after we see real customer usage patterns.

---

8) Appendix — raw benchmark table (representative)

Case | Range | Filters | Rows | CSV MB | JSON MB | CSV p50/p95 (s) | JSON p50/p95 (s)

B1 | 31d | env+region | 92k | 31 | 71 | 41.8 / 79.5 | 96.7 / 168.2
C1 | 31d | env only | 210k | 68 | 151 | 122.4 / 206.9 | 248.2 / >300 (timeout)
